patent_grounding.rationale: Revision 4 removes the shaft-drive assertion from both SJS descriptions and assumptions. Assumptions[1] explicitly disclaims inferring a drive source or shaft-drive function. Cited claim evidence supports attachment and impeller rotation inside the volute. The impeller flow-path description is supported by the patent description of liquid flowing via balancing holes to the rear-vane area.

functional_completeness.rationale: The flat component model includes the named volute, rear wall, shaft, and impeller assembly. The impeller description captures supported balancing-hole geometry and flow purpose. No drive-source subsystem is established in the cited patent and omission is appropriate.

flow_consistency.rationale: No typed item flows or flow interfaces are asserted. The descriptive hole path toward the rear-vane area is consistent with the patent description and avoids a fabricated boundary flow connection.

claim_traceability.rationale: Model captures the independent-claim component/attachment and front-opening relative placement attributes. Omitting dependent-claim geometric refinements is reasonable.

interfaces.rationale: The shaft-impeller interface connects existing mechanical_rotational ports, once, and represents the expressly supported attachment/rotation relation. It does not assert that the shaft drives the impeller.

textbook_application.rationale: Textbook modeling guidance informs system decomposition and restraint in defining interfaces only; invention facts are grounded in patent passages. No unsupported controls, external components, or requirements have been added.

summary: Revision 4 resolves the sole prior finding: no unsupported shaft-drive assertion remains in the SJS or assumptions. Patent passages support the shaft-impeller attachment/rotation relationship and the balancing-hole flow description; no further actionable issues found in the reviewed categories.
